issues.description: Missing input validation: 'text' parameter is not validated for empty, null, or undefined values. This will create todos with invalid/empty text that may break UI rendering or cause downstream errors.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the start of the function: `if (!text || typeof text !== 'string' || text.trim() === '') { throw new Error('Todo text must be a non-empty string'); }`

issues.description: ID generation uses array length which creates duplicate IDs when todos are removed. If a todo is deleted, the next added todo may reuse the same ID, causing data integrity issues and potential UI bugs (e.g., two todos with id=5).
issues.suggestion: Use a proper ID generation strategy: pass in a `getNextId` function, use `Math.max(...todos.map(t => t.id), 0) + 1`, or use a UUID library like `crypto.randomUUID()` for guaranteed uniqueness.

issues.description: Function mutates the input array directly by calling `todos.push()`, violating immutability principles. This makes the code harder to test, debug, and reason about, and can cause unexpected side effects in React/Redux applications.
issues.suggestion: Return a new array instead: `return [...todos, { id: todos.length + 1, text, done: false }];` This maintains immutability and makes the function pure.

issues.description: Missing parameter type validation or JSDoc documentation. The function signature doesn't indicate that 'todos' should be an array or what shape todo objects should have.
issues.suggestion: Add JSDoc comments: `/** @param {Array<{id: number, text: string, done: boolean}>} todos - Array of todo items @param {string} text - Text for the new todo @returns {Array} Updated todos array */`

issues.description: No validation that 'id' parameter exists or is the correct type. Calling with null, undefined, or wrong type will silently fail to remove the intended todo.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: `if (typeof id !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(id)) { throw new Error('Todo ID must be an integer'); }`

issues.description: Using loose inequality (t.id !== id) could lead to type coercion issues if IDs are sometimes strings and sometimes numbers. This is a common source of subtle bugs.
issues.suggestion: While !== is strict, ensure IDs are always the same type. Consider adding a comment or validation that enforces ID types consistently throughout the application.

issues.description: No error handling for edge cases: What happens if 'todos' is null, undefined, or not an array? The function will crash with a runtime error instead of providing a helpful error message.
issues.suggestion: Add defensive checks: `if (!Array.isArray(todos)) { throw new TypeError('First parameter must be an array of todos'); }`

issues.description: No error handling in removeTodo: If 'todos' is null, undefined, or not an array, this will crash at runtime instead of failing gracefully.
issues.suggestion: Add defensive checks: `if (!Array.isArray(todos)) { throw new TypeError('First parameter must be an array of todos'); }`

codeQuality.summary: The code has critical issues that will cause data integrity problems in production. The most severe issue is the ID generation bug (line 3) that creates duplicate IDs after deletions, which will break todo management. Additionally, the addTodo function mutates input arrays, violating immutability principles common in modern JavaScript frameworks. Both functions lack input validation, making them fragile and prone to runtime crashes with invalid inputs. The code needs defensive programming practices, proper ID generation, and immutability patterns before merging.
